meta.title: Holiday Guide
meta.subtitle: Shop Local For Gifts And More

businesses.name: Balsam Hollow Tree Farm
businesses.blurb: Cut-your-own balsams, a wood stove that never goes out, and free cider for anyone who carries their own tree.

businesses.name: Sugarplum Bakehouse
businesses.blurb: Stollen, gingerbread cottages, and a saffron bun the neighborhood queues around the block for.

businesses.name: Kettle & Kringle
businesses.blurb: Drinking chocolate thick enough to stand a spoon in, plus peppermint marshmallows toasted to order.

businesses.name: The Tinsel Tinker
businesses.blurb: A two-person workshop turning out wooden trains, tin robots, and rocking horses with terrible attitudes.

businesses.name: Frost Fair Market
businesses.blurb: Forty wooden chalets of makers, mulled wine, and one very committed brass band.

businesses.name: Glowworm Lights Co.
businesses.blurb: Vintage bulbs, hand-blown baubles, and a repair bench for the strand your grandmother refused to throw out.

businesses.name: The Nutmeg Nook
businesses.blurb: Spice merchants since 1948. Buy cinnamon by the stick and leave smelling like a pie.

businesses.name: Silver Bells Fine Trim
businesses.blurb: Ribbon by the yard, garlands by the fathom, and a bow-tying lesson with every order over a dollar.

businesses.name: Wassail Works
businesses.blurb: Hot spiced cider on tap, sold by the growler. Bring the pot, they'll fill it.

businesses.name: Reindeer Rest Stables
businesses.blurb: Sleigh rides through the orchard, hay bales optional, hot chestnuts absolutely mandatory.

businesses.name: The Paper Partridge
businesses.blurb: Letterpress cards, gift wrap you'll feel guilty tearing, and a mailbox straight to the North Pole.

businesses.name: Mistletoe Mercantile
businesses.blurb: Stocking stuffers, wind-up nonsense, and a penny-candy counter run entirely on the honor system.
